newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London weak, banks feature.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London weak, banks feature.

text.p: Hong Kong shares trading in London were lower across the board on Monday, with most interest centred on bank stocks after Hang Seng Bank reported disappointing company results, traders said.
"The market has been reasonably steady all day," said one trader. "The weak point is Hang Seng bank which has brought the index down more than anything else. "
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was 73.48 points lower at 13,433.8 points by 1447 GMT. A lower opening on the Dow had dragged the index to its lows of the day.
In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng closed with a gain of 108.56 points, or 0.81 percent, at 13,507.28 points. Property issues took centre stage, bouncing back from a period of underperformance.
"There's been no real follow-through on property stocks," a dealer said. "All the interest has been in the banking sector,"
Hang Seng Bank which is 61 percent owned by HSBC Holdings, reported annual net profit of HK$8.49 billion, down from HK$7.98 billion a year ago.
"The figures were disappointing," said the dealer, adding that other sectors in the market were relatively inactive.
Shares in Hang Seng were trading at HK$86.125 in London after a Hong Kong close of HK$89.
